subject: KPMG's AI report becomes an accidental demo of AI hallucinations
posts: KPMG's latest AI report is a masterclass in 'vibe citing,' proving that even the Big Four can fall victim to the very hallucinations they warn their clients about. #AI #TechFail
KPMG claimed to provide a definitive, expert-led analysis on the state of agentic AI to guide corporate investment and strategy. Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 1.0) — Greater Good
The reality is a report riddled with fabricated citations and false case studies, undermining the firm's credibility and misleading the market. Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil
Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. The firm sold expertise but delivered a hallucinated product, prioritizing speed and 'AI-first' optics over basic research integrity.
A forensic review by GPTZero found that only 5 of 45 citations in KPMG's October 2025 AI report were accurate, exposing a systemic failure in the firm's internal validation processes.

The Poison:
The consulting industry's rush to monetize AI has led to a 'vibe-based' approach to research, where the appearance of innovation is valued more than the substance of the data.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in the HOW plane. KPMG used AI to generate content (HOW) without the required human oversight (WHO). It is a bait-and-switch: they sold 'expert insight' but provided 'automated fiction.'

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between the promise of expert authority and the reality of AI-generated errors...
...it plots a trajectory toward Greater Evil, where the erosion of truth in professional services is accelerated by the very tools meant to enhance them.

The Unavoidable Truth: When experts outsource their thinking to AI, they lose the right to call themselves experts.

The Unavoidable Lie: That AI can replace the rigorous, human-led verification required for professional-grade research.

Alethekanon:
This is a failure of institutional rigor. KPMG has demonstrated that the 'AI-first' mandate, when applied without human validation, is a direct threat to the firm's core value proposition: trust.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see such a respected firm lose its way. We rely on these reports for guidance, and when that trust is broken by laziness, it hurts everyone who is trying to navigate this new tech landscape.

Brothekanon:
KPMG: 'We're the experts on AI.' Also KPMG: 'Let's have the AI write the report about how great AI is.' And then they're surprised when the AI makes up half the facts. You can't make this stuff up—but apparently, the AI can.
